newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia forecasts lower economic growth.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia forecasts lower economic growth.

text.p: Malaysia's gross domestic product (GDP) is expected to grow by 8.2 percent in 1996 and 8.0 percent in 1997 against 9.5 percent last year, the Finance Ministry said on Friday in its Economic Report for 1996/97.
The report said the government revised 1996 GDP growth from 8.3 percent projected earlier.
"Following a period of rapid expansion in the last eight years, the Malaysian economy is estimated to expand at a more sustainable pace in 1996," the report said.
A favourable international trading environment and continued expansion in the domestic manufacturing sector in 1997 will help maintain the pace of growth achieved this year, it said.

This would help the country's per capita income to grow by 10.5 percent to 11,118 ringgit ($4,447) and by another 9.5 percent in 1997 to 12,171 ringgit. In 1995, it grew by 11.8 percent to 10,058 ringgit, the report said.
Manufacturing would continue to be the main source of growth, with output projected to grow by 12.8 percent in 1996 and 12.5 percent next year against 14.5 percent in 1995.
Growth in the construction sector would moderate further to 8.8 percent in 1997 after growing at an estimated 9.0 percent in 1996 and an actual 17.3 percent in 1995, the report said.
Agriculture, forestry and fishing is forecast to grow 1.4 percent in 1997 from 1.6 percent in 1996 and 1.1 in 1995.
Mining is forecast to grow only 0.9 percent in 1997 from 3.1 percent in 1996 and 9.0 percent in 1995.
The financial year is the calendar year in Malaysia.
